concerns.concern: The review says a simpler explanation is not tested. Across all states higher T_c goes with higher sheet resistance and lower mobility, and prior KTO(111) work found T_c tracks mobility/disorder. If T_c collapses onto one mobility or disorder scaling curve for both gate-cycled and illuminated states, the PNR-mediated pairing picture is unnecessary.
concerns.quote: If T_c vs. μ (or vs. R_s, k_F·l) collapses onto a single curve for both gate-cycled and illuminated states, the PNR-mediated pairing picture is unnecessary.

concerns.concern: There is no direct evidence of polar-nanoregion alignment or remnant polarization: no P–E loops, PFM/SHG, Raman/IR soft-mode or structural probes. The central link between superconductivity and PNR alignment is asserted rather than measured, and no direct oxygen-vacancy charge-state probe is given.
concerns.quote: The key statement that "superconductivity and PNR alignment are strengthened by gate cycling and suppressed by illumination" is asserted rather than measured.

concerns.concern: The T_c change (~50–80 mK) is small, a fraction of the 0.2–0.3 K transition width. Because T_c is defined at 50% of a normal-state resistance that itself shifts by 5–8%, part of the shift may be a normalization artefact. Onset, zero-resistance and normalized-curve analyses with error estimates are missing.
concerns.quote: Part of the apparent shift may therefore reflect normal-state normalization rather than a change in pairing.

concerns.concern: The claimed "complete erasure" is not demonstrated. Illumination is never shown to return T_c or R_s to the pristine pre-gating value at the same temperature. Baselines are compared at different temperatures or against an already-cycled state, and the Discussion admits incomplete recovery.
concerns.quote: The manuscript never shows that illumination returns T_c (or R_s at the same temperature) to the pristine, pre-gating value.

concerns.concern: The thermally activated dielectric loss peaks could be Maxwell–Wagner/space-charge artefacts. Possible sources are the Au/KTO Schottky contact, the depletion layer, the AlOx, or defect hopping. The analysis also neglects the 2DEG sheet resistance and wiring; an equivalent-circuit or Cole–Cole analysis and a bare-substrate reference are needed.
concerns.quote: These alternatives are not ruled out; the analysis also neglects the finite 2DEG sheet resistance (~800 Ω) and the wiring.

concerns.concern: The carrier-density response to gating has the opposite sign to a conventional field effect. It is also several times larger than the capacitive estimate, and it is inconsistent with the post-illumination behaviour in Fig. 2g. None of this is discussed, although it is central to any charge-transfer model.
concerns.quote: These sign and magnitude inconsistencies are central to any charge-transfer model and need explicit treatment.

concerns.concern: The capacitance measurement averages over the whole 0.5 mm substrate rather than probing the near-interface region. The extracted permittivity (~1500–2000) is well below bulk KTO values, suggesting series dead or depletion layers or geometric errors that would distort tan δ.
concerns.quote: This suggests series dead layers or depletion regions and/or geometric/fringe errors.

concerns.concern: The correlation between hysteresis amplitude Δ_L and permittivity is weak evidence, since both are monotonic in temperature. The claimed deviation at 35 K and onset at 95 K rest on a handful of points. The sweep-rate dependence of Δ_L, needed for a kinetic interpretation, is not provided.
concerns.quote: Δ_L and ε are both monotonic functions of temperature, so a near-linear parametric plot (Fig. 3d) is weak evidence of causal coupling.

concerns.concern: The dark-relaxation time data contradict the text. The text claims τ minima at 35 K and 95 K, but 95 K is actually a sharp local maximum and adjacent points jump by ~50%. There are no error bars, and the single-exponential fit is not justified against stretched-exponential forms.
concerns.quote: The plotted data show τ minima near ~30–35 K and ~85–90 K, while 95 K is a sharp local *maximum* (~1.38×10³ s).

concerns.concern: The dielectric loss peaks are weakly identified on noisy, sloped curves, and the Arrhenius fits lack uncertainties. The assignment of the peaks to PNR reorientation and oxygen-vacancy ionization rests only on numerical matches to literature values.
concerns.quote: The assignment of Peak 2 to OV ionization rests solely on a numerical match to literature (200–300 meV)

concerns.concern: Single-band Hall analysis at ±6 T may not correctly separate density and mobility in a multi-band 2DEG when band occupations change. The reported changes are only ~1–5%, and the data lack error bars and demonstrated run-to-run reproducibility. Multi-band fits of field-dependent data are needed.
concerns.quote: Single-band Hall analysis at ±6 T in a multi-band KTO(111) 2DEG may not separate n and μ correctly when relative band occupations change.

concerns.concern: All data appear to come from a single device. There is no sample-to-sample reproducibility check and no dependence on AlOx thickness, reduction conditions, orientation or capping layer.
concerns.quote: All data appear to come from one sample.

concerns.concern: Illumination dose and LED heating are uncontrolled, because LED flux varies with temperature. The temperature dependence of relaxation magnitude and kinetics may therefore partly reflect varying dose rather than intrinsic physics.
concerns.quote: The temperature dependence of relaxation magnitude and kinetics may therefore partly reflect varying illumination dose and LED heating (visible at 2 K in Fig. 2b).

concerns.concern: The ΔR/R₁ maxima at 35 K and 95 K each rest on essentially a single data point. Denser temperature sampling around 30–40 K and 85–100 K is needed.
concerns.quote: The maxima at 35 K and 95 K (Fig. 4b) each rest on essentially a single data point.

concerns.concern: The dielectric loss and permittivity are not measured under dc gate bias or after illumination. If the peaks reflect the PNRs and oxygen vacancies behind the memory effect, they should change with the imprinted state.
concerns.quote: If the peaks reflect PNRs and OVs relevant to the memory, they should change with the imprinted state.

concerns.concern: Transport kinetics and dielectric relaxation are linked only by coinciding temperatures. Their microscopic timescales, including those from the Arrhenius analysis, are not compared quantitatively.
concerns.quote: so that common microscopic timescales are compared quantitatively rather than only by coincident temperatures.

concerns.concern: Device relevance and the memristive/neuromorphic framing are overstated. Erasure requires warming to 10 K and the gate needs ±50 V across 0.5 mm. No analog weights, endurance, retention statistics or switching energy are shown in the superconducting state.
concerns.quote: The abstract and conclusions thus extrapolate well beyond the data.

concerns.concern: Novelty is limited and the positioning relative to prior work is inadequate. Gate-cycling T_c enhancement (Ref. 30), hysteretic back-gating of KTO(111) and persistent photoconductivity are already reported.
concerns.quote: position the work more carefully relative to Ref. 30 and prior hysteretic gating studies on KTO.

concerns.concern: Perpendicular and parallel upper critical field data are missing. These would give coherence length and 2D thickness and help distinguish pairing changes from confinement or disorder changes.
concerns.quote: Add perpendicular/parallel H_c2 data, from which coherence length and possible changes in 2D thickness can be extracted.

concerns.concern: Sweep rates, hold times and gate-leakage levels are missing from the main-text measurement protocols.
concerns.quote: Sweep rates, hold times and gate-leakage levels are missing from the main-text protocols.

concerns.concern: There are presentation errors: a duplicated sentence, a mislabelled R_s value in Supp. Note 4, Fig. 3 caption inconsistencies with the text, inconsistent figure naming, and typos.
concerns.quote: In Supp. Note 4 (group 2), the elevated value is mislabelled R_s^b = 856 Ω
